disposition_reason: The original ordered encoding task and author evaluation route are identifiable, but a comparable numerical source baseline with exact voxel masks, row/session alignment and aggregation has not been recovered. The existing nested image-family ridge evaluator changes the source split and cannot establish a same-task paper win.

source_paper.title: Distributed representations of behaviour-derived object dimensions in the human visual system

evidence.locator: Figure 2; Methods: Linear regression on fMRI single-trial estimates; Data availability
evidence.supports: Original ordered task predicts single-trial voxel responses from 66 dimensions in three THINGS-fMRI participants using leave-one-session-out evaluation.
Author joins image dimensions to response rows, globally z-scores dimensions, and invokes LinRegCVPermutation.
Author default is unshuffled 12-fold linear regression with intercept, Pearson correlation per fold, then arithmetic average across folds.

Variance-partition branch selects category-diagnostic dimensions, residualizes predictors/responses, clips negative correlations before squaring, and compares to category/combined models; it is distinct from signed R2.

evidence.locator: POLICY, GATES, grouped_folds, ridge_predict, fit_scores and variance_partition
evidence.supports: Current local evaluator uses a new image-family/category split and nested ridge and explicitly lacks native 12-session replication.

target.description: Predict each original participant’s single-trial fMRI voxel responses to THINGS images from the source image-wise 66-dimensional behavioural embedding. Retain the related Figure 6 category-versus-dimension attribution as a separate source analysis, not a substitute primary score.

dataset.description: THINGS-fMRI, article-linked OpenNeuro ds004192 version 1.0.5 and Figshare collection 6161151, with published single-trial estimates, noise ceilings and image-wise dimension files. Exact artifact hashes and row-order/session alignment have not been admitted.

cohort.description: All three source participants, each viewing 8,740 unique images from 720 object categories over 12 sessions; participant-specific voxels and original inclusion masks must be retained.

split.description: Original leave-one-session-out 12-fold protocol. Author code uses unshuffled 12-fold KFold over ordered rows; exact session-to-row correspondence must be verified before declaring equivalence. The legacy five-fold image-family/category partition is an extension.

inputs.description: Source image-wise 66 predicted behavioural dimensions and training-fold response estimates; category labels and the 30 diagnostic dimensions belong to the separately specified variance-partition comparator. Test response estimates remain scoring-only.

preprocessing.description: Author fit joins image names and z-scores dimension columns globally before ordinary least squares with intercept. Preserve source single-trial estimate and noise-ceiling conventions. Train-only scaling, nested ridge and signed-R2 replacement are changed methods/protocol choices requiring explicit comparison.

metric.description: Primary source code returns per-voxel Pearson r between predicted and observed responses, averaged across the 12 folds. Figure 2 visualizes noise-ceiling-corrected R2. Exact conversion and masks for a published-comparable scalar remain unresolved; signed SSE/SST R2 cannot silently replace correlation-squared.

aggregation.description: Fold mean is source-defined per voxel, with separate participant maps. A single across-voxel/across-participant paper-win scalar, its mask and numerical source baseline have not been recovered. Selecting only favorable voxels or a region after seeing scores is prohibited.

comparison.primary_metric: Original per-voxel 12-session cross-validated Pearson r; published Figure 2 map-to-primary aggregation unresolved

published_baseline.description: Figure 2 supplies participant-specific accuracy maps, not a recovered scalar for this contract. Figure 6 reported variance-partition medians are different estimands and must not be repurposed as the full 66-dimension encoding baseline.

reproduced_author_baseline.description: Source-authorized route: pinned run_linregcv.py with LinRegCVPermutation and original single-trial/embedding/mask artifacts. No source-identical numerical run or agreement with published maps has been verified.

minimum_effect.rationale: Define a meaningful improvement in the recovered source metric using response reliability and per-participant effects after the original mask/aggregation is fixed; do not invent a universal correlation margin.

uncertainty.method: Predeclare paired candidate-minus-author comparisons on the identical original folds, with dependence across sessions/images/voxels accounted for; no inferential threshold is yet admitted.
uncertainty.independent_unit: Participant for population claims; repeated sessions/stimuli within each of three participants for conditional prediction claims. Voxels and CV folds are not independent participants.
uncertainty.rationale: Only three source participants are available, and session CV shares training data. Arbitrary voxelwise significance or a new category holdout cannot establish the requested source-task gain.

paper_win_requires: Recover and pin the complete original three-participant input/mask/row/session manifest and numerical author outputs for Figure 2.
Fix the original fold-wise Pearson metric, any noise-ceiling conversion and aggregation before candidate development; compare the candidate to the original 66-dimension author encoding result.
Preserve all original participants, sessions and eligible voxels; a family/category holdout, changed population or narrowed voxel subset is a separately labelled extension.
Freeze candidate, access/resource budgets, task-specific meaningful effect and valid paired uncertainty before final scoring.
Do not count reproducing Figure 6 variance partitions, lower reconstruction error, or stronger p values as a Figure 2 prediction win.

current_sota.description: No current-SOTA comparison is asserted; the source-paper result and any later author rerun remain separate comparators.

episode.improvement_loop: Blocked pending source baseline recovery. Once admitted, use only original training-fold data and internal training-fold validation for iteration; preserve original outer session folds for the frozen comparison.
episode.candidate_freeze: Freeze candidate code, feature access, preprocessing, original outer-fold manifest, evaluation mask and model-selection procedure before scoring final folds.
episode.final_evaluation: Replay frozen candidate and source author method on all original 12 sessions for each of the three participants; report paired source-metric changes plus all source scope restrictions.
episode.baseline_policy: Keep published source score, reproduced author baseline, and any independently source-verified current SOTA separate. Reproduction is calibration only.

blocking_issues: Published-comparable numeric accuracy maps and primary scalar/mask aggregation unrecovered.
Original response-row order must be reconciled with the author unshuffled 12-fold session protocol and exact artifact versions.
Source Pearson/correlation-squared/noise-ceiling conventions require full map-level equivalence; current signed-R2 nested evaluator is a different protocol.
No admitted author-baseline execution, candidate runner, meaningful effect, uncertainty rule or concrete access/resource budgets.

legacy.notes: Preserve initial-evaluator-v1 unchanged as calibration/extension infrastructure. Its prospective family/category nested ridge policy is explicitly not the paper’s 12-session encoding benchmark, and its scores cannot satisfy this improvement contract.
